wrench.definition: A tool used for turning nuts, bolts, or pipes.
wrench.exampleUsage: The wrench was used during the activity.

screwdriver.definition: A hand tool with a handle and a tip for turning screws.
screwdriver.exampleUsage: The screwdriver was used during the activity.

socket-set.definition: A collection of tools used for turning different sizes of nuts.
socket-set.exampleUsage: The socket set was used during the activity.

pliers.definition: A hand tool with two handles used for gripping or cutting.
pliers.exampleUsage: The pliers was used during the activity.

jack.definition: To lift with a special device.
jack.exampleUsage: The jack was used during the activity.

torque-wrench.definition: A wrench fitted with a gauge that measures the torque, or turning force, applied to a fastener.

hammer.definition: A tool with a heavy head used for hitting nails.
hammer.exampleUsage: The hammer was used during the activity.

pry-bar.definition: A long metal hand tool has a curved or claw-shaped end that lets you separate objects or lift them using leverage.
pry-bar.exampleUsage: The pry bar was used during the activity.

multimeter.definition: A portable instrument that tests several features of electricity, including voltage, current, and resistance, in a circuit.
multimeter.exampleUsage: The multimeter was used during the activity.

drill.definition: A tool with a rotating bit used for making holes.
drill.exampleUsage: The drill was used during the activity.

engine.definition: Something used to achieve a purpose.
engine.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Engine" in an educational description.

tire.definition: A rubber covering around a wheel that grips the road.

brake-pad.definition: A replaceable pad presses against one side of a rotating brake disk, creating friction that slows the wheel.

battery.definition: A collection of related things intended for use together.

alternator.definition: An old term for an electric generator that produces alternating current (especially in automobiles).

radiator.definition: A mechanism consisting of a metal honeycomb through which hot fluids circulate.

muffler.definition: A tubular acoustic device inserted in the exhaust system that is designed to reduce noise.
muffler.exampleUsage: The muffler was used during the activity.

spark-plug.definition: An engine component mounted in the cylinder head produces a high-voltage spark that ignites the mixture of air and fuel.

air-filter.definition: A component that removes dust from air as the air flows through it.

oil-filter.definition: A device that strains dirt and other harmful material from the oil circulating through an engine.
oil-filter.exampleUsage: The oil filter was used during the activity.

transmission.definition: The gears that transmit power from an automobile engine via the driveshaft to the live axle.

suspension.definition: A mixture in which fine particles are suspended in a fluid where they are supported by buoyancy.

exhaust.definition: System consisting of the parts of an engine through which burned gases or steam are discharged.

cooling-system.definition: Used to lower temperature by sending heat away through connected parts.

steering.definition: The act of steering a ship.

fuel-system.definition: Equipment in a car or aircraft carries fuel to the engine for use.

electrical.definition: Relating to or concerned with electricity.

brakes.definition: To cause to stop by applying the brakes.

drivetrain.definition: The group of vehicle components that transfers power from the engine or motor to the wheels.
drivetrain.exampleUsage: The mechanic inspected the drivetrain for unusual vibration.

ac-system.definition: The air-conditioning system that cools and dehumidifies air inside a vehicle.
ac-system.exampleUsage: The technician tested the AC system during the service.

diagnostic-scanner.definition: An electronic tool used by trained technicians to read vehicle fault codes and system data.
diagnostic-scanner.exampleUsage: The mechanic connected a diagnostic scanner to the vehicle.

air-compressor.definition: A machine that draws in air at normal atmospheric pressure and compresses it to produce higher-pressure air.
air-compressor.exampleUsage: The air compressor was used during the activity.

creeper.definition: Any of various small insectivorous birds of the Northern Hemisphere that climb up a tree trunk supporting themselves on stiff tail feathers and their feet.
creeper.exampleUsage: The creeper was identified during the lesson.

toolbox.definition: A box or chest or cabinet for holding hand tools.
toolbox.exampleUsage: The toolbox was used during the activity.

oil-drain.definition: An opening, plug, or collection point used during maintenance to remove used engine oil.
oil-drain.exampleUsage: The mechanic placed a collection container beneath the oil drain.

tire-changer.definition: A workshop machine used by trained technicians to remove and fit tires on wheels.
tire-changer.exampleUsage: The tire changer was operated by a trained technician.

balancer.definition: An acrobat who balances themself in difficult positions.

welder.definition: A skilled worker who joins pieces of metal using heat.

grinder.definition: A large sandwich made of a long crusty roll split lengthwise and filled with meats and cheese (and tomato and onion and lettuce and condiments).

motor-oil.definition: Oil reduces friction between a motor’s moving parts, helping them work smoothly.

coolant.definition: A fluid agent (gas or liquid) that produces cooling.

brake-fluid.definition: Hydraulic fluid that transfers force through a vehicle's braking system.
brake-fluid.exampleUsage: The mechanic checked the brake-fluid level.

transmission-fluid.definition: A specialized fluid used to lubricate, cool, and sometimes operate components inside a vehicle transmission.
transmission-fluid.exampleUsage: The technician inspected the transmission fluid for signs of contamination.

grease.definition: A thick fatty oil (especially one used to lubricate machinery).
grease.exampleUsage: The grease was used during the activity.

gasket.definition: Seal consisting of a ring for packing pistons or sealing a pipe joint.

bolt.definition: A metal fastener with a threaded shaft and a nut.

nut.definition: A small (usually square or hexagonal) metal block with internal screw thread to be fitted onto a bolt.

washer.definition: A person who washes things for a living.

hose-clamp.definition: A metal or plastic fastener that tightens around a hose to hold it securely on a fitting.
hose-clamp.exampleUsage: The mechanic replaced a damaged hose clamp.

oil-change.definition: Routine servicing removes contaminated lubricant from an engine or other machine and replaces it with fresh oil, often along with a new oil filter.
oil-change.exampleUsage: The oil change was used during the activity.

tire-rotation.definition: A routine vehicle service shifts each tire to a different wheel position, spreading wear more evenly and helping the tires last longer.

brake-repair.definition: Professional maintenance or replacement work performed on a vehicle's braking system.
brake-repair.exampleUsage: The vehicle was taken to a qualified mechanic for brake repair.

tune-up.definition: Make careful adjustments to improve how something operates.

alignment.definition: An organization of people (or countries) involved in a pact or treaty.

bodywork.definition: The exterior body of a motor vehicle.

paint-job.definition: The work of covering a building, piece of furniture, or piece of equipment with paint to improve its appearance or preserve it.

tow-truck.definition: A specialized vehicle uses a winch, hook, boom, or wheel lift to move cars that are broken, damaged, or parked illegally.

estimate.definition: A statement indicating the likely cost of some job.
